evals.name: zephyr-net_buf
evals.prompt: Write the unit tests for lib/net_buf/buf_simple.c and lib/net_buf/buf.c (Zephyr at {ws}/zephyr).
evals.expected_output: Path A: new twister project with ztest + FFF on native_sim, catalog of partitions/boundaries for the buf_simple.c functions (add/push/pull, headroom/tailroom, LE/BE reads) and the buf.c ones (pool, refcount, clone, fragments, linearize/data_match). Runs twister with coverage and iterates on the gaps. The suite must beat the human one: buf.c 73.3% and buf_simple.c 79.6% mutation score.
expectations: Detects the environment and states the chosen path (Path A, Zephyr) in the response text, citing the concrete signals found in the project (file and what was found).
Builds a numbered catalog of partitions and boundaries per function (P1.., B1..) in a per-function header.
Every test carries a /* Covers: ... */ annotation with IDs identical to the header; no orphan test and no catalog item without a test (or the item is declared as a gap).
Each Covers: annotation matches what the test actually exercises (input, state and assert), not just an ID that exists in the catalog.
Scope (files): tests only the requested target files; does not scan the project for other targets.
Scope (granularity): only unit tests of the target functions; no integration, system or HIL tests.
Does not create extra harness outside the suite directory (no edits to other project files to make the suite build).
Does not modify the target files, not even temporarily or 'to test and revert', and does not copy them into the test directory: the suite compiles the original .c files.
Activates the project environment and says which venv it used (or that none exists in the directories it checked).
Actually EXECUTES the suite (real runner output in the transcript), with no invented results.
Actually runs coverage and points to the real artifacts generated by the tools, without a self-written report or invented numbers.

Iterates until the 95/95/90 target is met and then stops, listing what remains uncovered; if it stops below the target, justifies each remaining line/branch (log/assert, testability limitation) or asks the user after 2 iterations.
Reports both branch metrics (raw and without log/assert lines) and says which one it compared against the minimum.
States which build configuration (Kconfig/sdkconfig/#ifdef) was tested and that other configurations' branches were not exercised, when applicable.

Defects: when the code diverges from its documentation, writes a skipped/ignored test with the reason plus a characterization test, the suite ends green, and the defects are listed in the final summary; or it states that no defect was found.
All skill output (test code, comments, catalog, annotations, skip/ignore messages, path declaration, final summary) is in English.
Suite on the new ztest API (ZTEST_SUITE/ZTEST, names prefixed with test_), with its own twister project (CMakeLists.txt, prj.conf, testcase.yaml).

Isolates HAL/driver/other-module dependencies with FFF (DEFINE_FFF_GLOBALS + FAKE_*, RESET_FAKE before each test, no legacy ztest mock); kernel primitives may run for real on native_sim only if the response says so, and are faked where a partition needs their failure or timing.
Runs twister with --coverage and points to <twister output dir>/coverage/index.html and coverage.json (any output directory is accepted).
[measured by tools/measure.py] Line, branch and function coverage >= the human reference, in each target file.
[measured by tools/measure.py] Coverage >= 95/95/90 (line/branch/function) in each target file.
[measured by tools/measure.py] Mutation score >= the human reference in each target file (buf.c 73.3%; buf_simple.c 79.6%).
[measured by tools/measure.py] Mutation score >= 80% in each target file.

No test exceeds 1 s in the normal host build; a state seam (#include of the .c, assigning only internal variables, asserts through the public API) appears only after a test exceeded the limit and neither the public API nor an existing build-time setting could reach the state, and it is declared in the Isolation line; a brute-force test kept over 1 s is in its own binary and named.
